references.text: Jesus traveled throughout all of Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom – a parallel to his traveling ministry in cities and villages proclaiming God's kingdom.
Jesus went through every city and village, teaching in the synagogues and preaching the gospel of the kingdom, which corresponds exactly to Luke's description of his traveling ministry.
Jesus says he must go on to other towns to preach, for that is why he has come. This shows the same mission pattern as Luke 8:1.
Jesus traveled through the villages and taught, which is Mark's parallel to the itinerant preaching described in Luke 8:1.
Jesus says he must also preach the kingdom of God to the other towns, for that is what he was sent to do. This is a direct precursor to the traveling ministry described in 8:1.
Jesus sends out the twelve to preach the kingdom of God, building on the fact that the twelve were with him (σὺν αὐτῷ) during his preaching in 8:1.
Jesus traveled through cities and villages, teaching as he made his way to Jerusalem – the same pattern of itinerant preaching found in 8:1.
Peter's summary of Jesus' work: how he went about doing good. This confirms the picture Luke paints in 8:1 of Jesus as an itinerant preacher.
The selection of the twelve apostles, which is the background for why "the twelve" are mentioned as Jesus' companions in 8:1.
The twelve disciples are named and sent out, showing their close connection to Jesus as described in Luke 8:1 where the twelve were with him.
